resale_co.how_to_apply: No Borough Certificate of Occupancy is needed for a sale. Separately, the Borough requires a Department of Public Works water and sewer House Inspection before closing (see other_items) and a final meter read.
resale_co.contact_title: Superintendent of Public Works (schedules the pre-closing water and sewer House Inspection)

evidence.quote: The Borough does not require a Certificate of Occupancy for the sale of a residential property.
Please note that the Borough does not require a CO for the sale of residential properties.
This inspection may be scheduled by calling the Superintendent of Public Works, Rick Smith 609-737-9440, a minimum of ten business days before the closing date of the sale of your house.
Once you have a closing date email Gabrielle Smith, DPW ( publicworks@penningtonboro.org ), to schedule a final meter read.

resale_co.notes: The Borough Home Sale Checklist lists three steps: a DPW House Inspection (609-737-9440), the fire inspection through the NJ DCA portal, and a final meter read. The checklist PDF (July 2024) misspells the DPW email as 'penningotnboro.org'; the web page shows publicworks@penningtonboro.org. The DPW House Inspection is a water and sewer inspection, not a Certificate of Occupancy; its fee is in other_items.

authorities.name: NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement (State is the fire code enforcing agency and issues smoke certificates in Pennington)
authorities.lead_time: More than 10 business days before closing for the lowest fee

fees.label: Application more than 10 business days before closing
fees.quote: If you are applying for a certificate more than ten business days from the closing date the fee is $45 dollars

fees.label: Application 4 to 10 business days before closing
fees.quote: if applying 4 to 10 business days from the closing date the fee is $90

fees.label: Application less than 4 business days before closing
fees.quote: if the closing date is less than four business days the fee is $161.

fees.label: State rule: request received more than 10 business days before change of occupant (N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d), NJ Register October 2, 2017)
fees.quote: 1. Requests for a CSDCMAC received more than 10 business days prior to the change of occupant: $45.00;

fees.label: State rule: request received 4 to 10 business days before change of occupant (2017)
fees.quote: 2. Requests for a CSDCMAC received four to 10 business days prior to the change of occupant: $90.00; and

fees.label: State rule: request received fewer than 4 business days before change of occupant (2017)
fees.quote: 3. Requests for a CSDCMAC received fewer than four business days prior to the change of occupant: $161.00.

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply and pay online through the NJ DCA Fire Safety Service Portal ('Start Your Smoke Certification Application'), as the Borough checklist directs. Pay by e-check or credit card before submitting; a valid email is required and the certificate is emailed once the fee is paid and any required inspection is done. Homes heated only by electricity with no attached garage (no CO alarm needed) should email BFCE_CSDCMAC@dca.nj.gov.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Official for Pennington in the state directory (Bureau Chief, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement)

fire_cert.notes: Pennington Ordinance 2026-3 moved fire code enforcement from the Hopewell Township Fire Commissioners (Fire District No. 1) to the NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety, pending a Borough fire official for non-life-hazard uses. The July 2026 LEA registry lists the State (S), and the state list of State-enforced towns marks Pennington 'SC' (State issues smoke certificates). The state directory still carries a note 'SSA with Hopewell Twp FD#1'. The DCA fee sentences and the BFCE_CSDCMAC@dca.nj.gov address are in the DCA application page's own instructions (page source). The DCA application title now covers smoke alarms, CO alarms and the secondary power source label (no extinguisher). The DCA BFCE page lists Louis Kilmer at (609) 633-6106; the state directory lists (609) 633-6132 for Pennington.

other_items.label: Water and sewer House Inspection by the Department of Public Works (required before closing)
other_items.detail: Schedule at least ten business days before closing with Superintendent of Public Works Rick Smith, 609-737-9440. The Water/Sewer page says: 'There is a fee of $100 that must be either mailed or dropped off at Borough Hall before the inspection.' The Home Sale Checklist instead says the House Inspection fee is charged to the final water/sewer bill. Ordinance 2026-19 (introduced May 4, 2026; adoption not confirmed) sets 'House inspections on sale of property: regular fee' at $200 (was $150) and $300 (was $250) with less than 10 days' notice.

other_items.label: House inspection fee in Ordinance 2026-19 (introduced May 4, 2026)
other_items.detail: Quote: "House inspections on sale of property: regular fee, $150 $200; fee if less than 10 days' notice, $250 $300 ." In the ordinance, $150 and $250 are struck out and $200 and $300 are underlined (new).

other_items.label: Final water meter read
other_items.detail: Once there is a closing date, email Gabrielle Smith, DPW (publicworks@penningtonboro.org), with the title company name. A non-quarterly meter read fee is charged to the final water/sewer bill (Ordinance 2026-19 proposes $100 scheduled, up from $75).

open_questions: Which House Inspection fee applies now: $100 (Water/Sewer page), $150/$250 (current code per Ordinance 2026-19's struck text), or $200/$300 (Ordinance 2026-19, adoption not confirmed)? And is it paid up front or added to the final water/sewer bill?
